current_to_reconciled_exact_passage_acco.new_exact:
=== Earlier assessments and their limits ===

The earlier assessment stated: “No inspected record proves that Thomas was a son, brother, nephew or other relative of Archibald Glasgow M.A. (1614–bef.1677).” It allowed a son or younger relative of the Donegal clergyman whose will was proved in 1677, but described the Archibald–Thomas–Nathaniel line as unsupported by direct kinship evidence. That broad assessment is superseded in part by Betham’s abstract of the April 1673 will: the testator explicitly had an eldest son Thomas. What remains unproved is that son’s identity with the Lifford man and any Thomas–Nathaniel link. The age, Scottish origin and denomination attributed to Archibald require their own evidence; they do not follow from this abstract.

The former after-25-November-1695 death bound came from the £6,000 bond memorandum. It is superseded by the 15 May 1701 Exchequer entry already described above. The 1695 event remains valid evidence of his life and associations.

=== Search of the surviving registered will book ===

The surviving 1664–1684 prerogative will book is accessible. Its visible G index (image 542 of 547) and all nine full-text Glas* matches were checked on 30 September 2026 without locating Archibald’s particular will. The full manuscript has not been read, so this does not establish that the will is absent or destroyed.<ref>National Archives of Ireland, prerogative wills 1664–1684, FamilySearch DGS 8096787, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJ8-FDT8 image 542, G index].</ref>

current_to_proposed_exact_passage_accoun.new_exact:
=== Working father connection ===

Robert and Samuel belong to the same documented sibling group as [[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-3896|Daniel Glasgow]]. A descendant family account names [[Glasgow-3904|Alexander Glasgow of Lisnagaver]] as Thomas's father, and Thomas and Daniel are already attached to Alexander on that basis.<ref name="FatherTradition">Peter, “Trying to find Glasgow,” ''Genes Reunited'', [https://www.genesreunited.co.uk/boards/board/general_topics/thread/465937 discussion], descendant account naming Alexander and Rosanna as parents of Thomas Glasgow. This is family testimony rather than a contemporary parent record.</ref> Their proved brotherhood and compatible chronology support Alexander as an uncertain father of Robert and Samuel too. This connects the documented brothers through the existing family hypothesis; it does not make the father relationship certain. Rosanna's maternity is assessed separately and is not established by the sibling deeds.

current_to_reconciled_exact_passage_acco.old_exact: Samuel was a brother of Robert Glasgow, the Prescott shipbuilder. Robert's will, dated 9 October 1849, gives one sixth each to his brothers Daniel, Samuel, John and Thomas, his sister Mary, and collectively the children of his brother James; it does not call James deceased.<ref name="RobertWill1849">Grenville County land records, DGS 8200419, image 35, registered will of Robert Glasgow of Prescott, dated 9 October 1849, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWY9-S original image].</ref> Memorial 13 records a 30 October 1856 deed, registered 13 November 1856, by which Robert's widow Jane sold Samuel, merchant, property in which he held one undivided sixth share under Robert's will.<ref name="RobertWill1856">Grenville County land records, DGS 8200419, image 36, Memorial 13, dated 30 October 1856 and registered 13 November 1856, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWYM-6 original image].</ref> Memorial 465, dated 30 July 1861 and registered 7 October, names Daniel of Kilrea, County Londonderry, watchmaker, and wife Margaret, and Thomas of Lisnagaver, County Antrim, farmer, and wife Mary Ann, in transfers to Samuel of two undivided sixth interests under Robert's will.<ref name="RobertWill1861">Grenville County land records, DGS 8200419, image 240, Memorial 465, registered 7 October 1861, printed p. 397, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWB8-D original image].</ref> The deeds establish the stated Daniel, Thomas and Samuel as Robert's brothers by place, trade and wife; they do not identify the siblings' parents.

=== Household count and earlier relationship assessment ===

The earlier household reconstruction described “eight people appearing as children in 1851” and counted them with the two later sons as ten children. The cited census has eight household members, of whom six are probable children; that arithmetic is corrected above. The local-history report of ten children, six surviving, is retained as a separate attributed claim, not independently reconciled by the census.

The 2017 account’s father–son claim was initially treated as credible local-history evidence awaiting a contemporary deed or estate reading. The inspected will and memorials establish Robert as Samuel’s brother. An earlier caution requested a full reading of Robert’s will to explain the share fractions; the will is now read, while the identity of James the carpenter and the complete title chain still need resolution.

=== Working father connection ===

Robert and Samuel belong to the same documented sibling group as [[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-3896|Daniel Glasgow]]. A descendant family account names [[Glasgow-3904|Alexander Glasgow of Lisnagaver]] as Thomas's father, and Thomas and Daniel are already attached to Alexander on that basis.<ref name="FatherTradition">Peter, “Trying to find Glasgow,” ''Genes Reunited'', [https://www.genesreunited.co.uk/boards/board/general_topics/thread/465937 discussion], descendant account naming Alexander and Rosanna as parents of Thomas Glasgow. This is family testimony rather than a contemporary parent record.</ref> Their proved brotherhood and compatible chronology support Alexander as an uncertain father of Robert and Samuel too. This connects the documented brothers through the existing family hypothesis; it does not make the father relationship certain. Rosanna's maternity is assessed separately and is not established by the sibling deeds.
